title: ACCA FM - Financial Management
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the ACCA FM syllabus study guide. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A company is reviewing its financial management objectives. In a shareholder value maximisation approach, which action is most appropriate for the financial manager?
options: Focus decisions on increasing long-term shareholder wealth rather than short-term accounting profits alone
Maximise reported profit for the current year regardless of risk or capital investment requirements
Prioritise reducing tax liabilities over all other objectives to maximise distributable reserves
Maintain the highest possible dividend payout ratio at all times to satisfy shareholders directly
items.explanation: Shareholder wealth maximisation focuses on long-term value creation by considering cash flows, timing and risk, rather than short-term accounting profits.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which statement best describes the primary role of the financial manager in a listed company with separation of ownership and control?
options: To prioritise the personal objectives of directors over those of external investors at all times
To act as an agent for shareholders by making investment and financing decisions that maximise their wealth
To ensure that all operational decisions are taken without reference to capital constraints
To report only to operational managers and focus solely on cost control measures
items.explanation: The financial manager acts as an agent for shareholders, balancing investment, financing and dividend decisions to maximise shareholder wealth.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which factor is most likely to create an agency problem between shareholders and directors in a large public company?
options: All directors are required to own a majority shareholding in the company by statute
Dividends are automatically linked to director bonuses in every public limited company
Directors may pursue their own interests, such as increased remuneration, at the expense of shareholder wealth
Shareholders and directors always have identical time horizons for all investment projects
items.explanation: Agency problems arise when directors (agents) pursue personal goals that conflict with the objective of maximising shareholder wealth.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: In the context of financial management, which statement best describes the difference between profit maximisation and wealth maximisation?
options: Profit maximisation is always superior as it is based on audited financial statements
Wealth maximisation can only consider historical costs and does not account for future cash flows
There is no practical difference between the two objectives for decision making purposes
Wealth maximisation takes account of cash flows, timing and risk, whereas profit maximisation ignores these factors
items.explanation: Wealth maximisation considers the time value of money, risk and future cash flows, while profit maximisation focuses on accounting profit alone.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which of the following is most likely to be a key economic factor affecting financial management decisions in a domestic market?
options: Changes in interest rates and inflation rates impacting the cost of capital and cash flows
The choice of accounting policy for tangible fixed assets under IFRS only
The company's registered office address in relation to company law filings
The format of board meeting minutes as prescribed by the articles of association
items.explanation: Macroeconomic factors such as interest rates and inflation directly affect borrowing costs, discount rates and the real value of future cash flows.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which statement best describes the role of the money markets within the financial system?
options: They deal only with foreign exchange spot transactions between central banks
They facilitate the trading of short-term debt instruments with maturities typically less than one year
They provide a primary market for the issue of long-term equity only to institutional investors
They are exclusively used for trading physical commodities such as gold and oil futures
items.explanation: Money markets deal with short-term borrowing and lending, typically for periods of less than one year, through instruments such as treasury bills and commercial paper.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which of the following best distinguishes the capital markets from the money markets?
options: Capital markets are unregulated, whilst money markets are always regulated by the stock exchange
There is no distinction as both markets deal exclusively with derivatives
Capital markets facilitate long-term financing, whereas money markets focus on short-term funding
Money markets only trade equities, while capital markets only trade government debt
items.explanation: Capital markets provide long-term finance through equity and bonds, whereas money markets provide short-term finance through instruments with maturities under one year.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which statement best explains the difference between primary and secondary capital markets?
options: The primary market only trades derivatives, whilst the secondary market trades physical assets
Only the secondary market raises new capital for companies issuing shares or bonds
Both markets exclusively handle government securities with no corporate participation
The primary market is where new securities are issued, while the secondary market is where existing securities are traded
items.explanation: In the primary market, companies raise new capital by issuing securities directly to investors; in the secondary market, existing securities are traded between investors.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which of the following is most likely to be a disadvantage of operating as a public limited company compared to a private limited company?
options: Increased regulatory requirements and greater public disclosure of financial information
Complete inability to raise external finance from banks or other institutions
Permanent restriction on the number of shareholders to a maximum of ten individuals
Automatic exemption from all taxation on company profits and distributions
items.explanation: Public limited companies face stricter regulatory and disclosure requirements than private limited companies, increasing compliance costs and administrative burden.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: Which factor best explains why a company might choose to list its shares on a stock exchange?
options: To ensure that shareholder decisions can no longer be influenced by majority voting
To gain access to a wider pool of capital for growth and investment opportunities
To eliminate all financial risk associated with operating in its industry sector
To avoid paying any corporation tax on future profits generated after listing
items.explanation: Listing provides access to public capital markets, allowing companies to raise equity finance from a broad investor base to fund expansion and development.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Financial Management Function and Environment

items.stem: A company using Baumol model: if annual cash requirement increases, optimal cash balance?
items.explanation: Optimal cash rises with sqrt of requirement in Baumol.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Which of the following best describes how the Miller-Orr cash management model is used to control cash balances?
items.explanation: Miller-Orr manages random flows with control limits and return point.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: EOQ increases when? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: EOQ proportional to sqrt of demand.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Safety stock purpose? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Safety stock reduces stockout risk from variability.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: EOQ trade-off? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: EOQ balances placing orders against holding inventory.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Reduce receivables period? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Tighten credit control and early settlement discounts
items.explanation: Better control/discounts speed collection.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Cost of trade credit? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Credit ties up funds and risks irrecoverable debts.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Increase payables period? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Longer terms delay cash outflows.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Cash conversion cycle measures?
options: Time to convert WC to cash
items.explanation: CCC = inventory+receivables-payables, cash tied in ops.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Aggressive WC financing? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Uses cheaper short-term but higher refinancing risk.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Overdraft is? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Overdraft allows temporary overdraws.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Factoring? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Sell receivables for cash often with credit protection
items.explanation: Factor advances cash and may handle credit control.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Working Capital Management

items.stem: Investment appraisal: relevant cash flows?
items.explanation: Only future incremental flows affect decisions.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: NPV decision rule for independent project?
items.explanation: Positive NPV adds value to shareholders.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: IRR definition? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Rate of return on accounting profit
items.explanation: IRR equates PV of inflows to outflows.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Payback period limitation? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Simple payback ignores discounting.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Discounted payback advantage over payback?
items.explanation: Discounted payback discounts cash flows.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Mutually exclusive projects: ranking conflict?
items.explanation: Different scales/timings can give conflicting rankings; use NPV.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Capital rationing exists when?
items.explanation: Hard/soft rationing restricts capital.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Profitability index used for? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: PI = PV inflows/investment; useful for divisible projects under rationing.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Sensitivity analysis? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Change one variable to see NPV effect
items.explanation: Sensitivity tests impact of changing a single variable.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Scenario analysis? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: Scenarios assess combined effects.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Risk-adjusted discount rate? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
items.explanation: RADR increases discount rate to reflect risk.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Certainty equivalent approach?
options: Convert risky cash flows to certain equivalents
items.explanation: Certainty equivalents adjust cash flows rather than discount rate.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Real vs nominal discounting? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Match real/nominal rates to real/nominal cash flows
items.explanation: Consistency avoids double-counting inflation.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal

items.stem: Working capital in appraisal? Which of the following is the most appropriate explanation in line with the ACCA FM syllabus study guide?
options: Treated as investment at start and recovered at end
items.explanation: Working capital outflow initially, inflow at end of project.
items.reference: ACCA FM Syllabus Study Guide - Investment Appraisal
